title: A Fish Can Wait Out a Drought for Four Years in Mud

scenes.text: A fish can wait out a drought for four years.
It's the West African lungfish, and when its pond dries up, it digs in.
It burrows about ten inches into the mud and wraps itself in a cocoon of hardened mucus.
The cocoon keeps moisture in, and a primitive lung breathes air.
It stops eating and drinking, and slowly digests muscle from its own tail to stay alive.
Guinness lists four years without food. Then the rain comes.

description:
A fish can wait out a drought for four years.
The West African lungfish buries itself in mud and enters a cocoon, stopping eating and drinking until the rains refill its waterways.
Could you wait four years for rain? Comment below.
first_comment: How would the first rain feel after four years?
